propositions: A detached compaction sweep that dies between snapshot-write/retire and git commit leaves the tracker working tree dirty with tracked deletions and untracked snapshot/retired files, causing the next reconverge merge to abort and strand local commits.

The operation-linked compaction fold (snapshot-write → retire-rename → commit) lacks atomicity guarantees; failures at any step can leave the shared tracker in an inconsistent state without recovery path.

An intent journal + rollback + recovery pattern must be implemented to make compaction crash-atomic: write journal before mutations, perform ordered mutations with rollback on failure, and recover at sweep entry by discriminating abandoned folds (partial) from landed folds (journal-only cleanup).

Recovery probes must distinguish object-absent from transient git failures (index.lock, timeout) to avoid misclassifying a transient fault as a landed fold and incorrectly reverting committed snapshots.

Incomplete rollback (failing reverse-rename) must retain the uncommitted snapshot as SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT rather than delete it, preserving folded events for fsck repair; the journal is cleared without revisiting the snapshot.
